title: security-eng-sync-notes-2026-03-05
content:
Security Engineering Sync — 2026-03-05
Attendees: Lena Morales (note taker), Ravi Singh, Aisha Patel, Tomás García, Priya Kapoor, Ethan Wong

Agenda:
- Quick round robin (blockers/updates)
- Vulnerability triage: Open CVEs and prioritization
- Secrets hygiene: recent scanner findings and remediation plan
- Threat modeling: scope for Dedicated control plane changes
- Action items & owners

1) Round robin / updates (2–3 min each)
- Ravi: Finished PR for improved image scanning step in CI; staging run flagged 3 non-prod containers with outdated glibc. Will open follow-up to patch base images. Blocker: access to some internal images for SRE testing (SEC-418).
- Aisha: Finished draft of the secret scanning whitelist for vendor keys; requests review. Noted one false-positive pattern from legacy deploy scripts.
- Tomás: Observability: added tags to runtime logs to correlate request id with model variant; will help triage exploit investigation.
- Priya: Threat model kickoff scheduled for next Tue for Dedicated control plane changes; asked for any pre-read materials.
- Ethan: Incident playbook updates in progress (response runbooks for model escape and data exfil), need SME review on forensics steps.

2) Vulnerability triage
- New items since last sync: CVE-2026-0217 (dependency in tokenization library), medium priority; reproduces on dev but not on hosted infra. ACTION: Aisha to open SEC-424 with reproduction steps and suggested mitigation (pin to patched minor). Due: 2026-03-09.
- CVE-2026-0199 (CUDA driver compatibility issue) affecting Dedicated nodes on older GPU drivers; high priority for Dedicated customers on v1 pools. Decision: schedule immediate rolling upgrade of affected Dedicated pools during the next maintenance window. ACTION: Ravi to coordinate with infra and notify impacted customers via CS. JIRA: SEC-412. Due: 2026-03-07.
- Backlog triage: lower-severity findings from last week's dependency scan were deferred; team agreed to address in the April patch cycle unless they escalate.

3) Secrets hygiene
- Secret scanner summary (scan run 2026-03-04): 18 findings -> 12 false positives, 6 actionable (3 AWS keys, 2 service account JSONs, 1 Slack webhook).
- Immediate remediation plan: rotate exposed keys + confirm no suspicious usage. ACTIONS:
  - Ethan: rotate the 3 AWS keys and create incident log entries. Due: 2026-03-06.
  - Tomás: delete the Slack webhook and update the bot config to use the new webhook with least privilege. Due: 2026-03-06.
  - Aisha: add the two service account JSONs to the secrets manager and revoke the files from repo. Also add a scanner rule to reduce false positives for vendor key formats. Due: 2026-03-08.
- Policy change proposal: require pre-commit hook that runs lightweight secret scanning for all infra repos (non-blocking on feature branches; block on main). Team approves moving the RFC to product-ops. ACTION: Lena to draft RFC and post to #sec-policy by 2026-03-10.

4) Threat modeling: Dedicated control plane changes
- Context: product is introducing a multi-tenant routing layer for Dedicated to improve resource utilization. Concern: control plane API surface increases and could introduce privilege escalation if routing metadata is trusted incorrectly.
- Discussion points:
  - Trust boundaries: control plane vs. tenant agents; need stricter validation at the routing layer; do not accept opaque tenant-provided routing tokens without server-side verification.
  - Data classification: ensure routing metadata cannot carry customer-sensitive fields.
  - Failure modes: if the routing layer is compromised, attackers could route requests to arbitrary model variants or inject prompt prefixes.
- Decisions:
  - Threat modeling session scheduled for 2026-03-10, 11:00–12:30 PT. Priya to own facilitation and invite infra, runtime, and product-hosted-api reps.
  - Prep: everyone to review the control plane API spec (link in linked_artifacts) and bring a list of trust assumptions. ACTION: Priya to circulate pre-read by 2026-03-07.

5) Incidents and posture
- No active incidents. Postmortem follow-ups from Feb red-team exercise: improve canarying of rollout hooks and add chaos tests for KV cache invalidation. ACTION: Ravi to create ENGINF ticket to add chaos test harness. Due: 2026-03-20.

6) Action items recap (owner — due)
- Ravi: coordinate Dedicated driver rollout and customer comms (SEC-412) — 2026-03-07.
- Aisha: open SEC-424 for tokenization lib CVE + reduce false positives on vendor keys — 2026-03-09 / 2026-03-08.
- Ethan: rotate 3 AWS keys and log in incident tracker — 2026-03-06.
- Tomás: remove Slack webhook and update bot config — 2026-03-06.
- Priya: circulate threat model pre-read and run session on 2026-03-10 — 2026-03-07 / 2026-03-10.
- Lena: draft secrets policy RFC (pre-commit secret scanning) — 2026-03-10.
- Ravi: create ENGINF chaos test ticket for KV cache invalidation — 2026-03-20.

Open questions / parking lot:
- Should we treat vendor-provided deploy keys as immutable whitelisted tokens or require rotation on onboarding? (parking for policy discussion)
- How aggressive should secret scanning be for mono-repo with lots of infra scripts (false positive noise vs. coverage)?

Notes / links referenced during sync:
- JIRA SEC-412 (Dedicated driver compatibility)
- JIRA SEC-418 (image access for infra testing)
- GitHub runtime PR #2145 (logging tags change)
- Secret scan: gs://redwood-sec-reports/2026/03/secret-scan-2026-03-04.pdf

Next meeting: 2026-03-12 09:30 PT (weekly cadence)

-- end sync notes --
